ground_truth.title: State v. Thomas Keller
ground_truth.location: Portview, Harborview Law Partners office, 12th floor server room
ground_truth.charge: Unlawful access and removal of confidential client data

defendant.name: Thomas Keller
defendant.background: Long-time union member with no prior criminal record; recently unemployed due to dock layoffs; has outstanding debt

victim.name: Harborview Law Partners
victim.description: Mid-size law firm specializing in maritime and corporate litigation

ground_truth.what_really_happened: On June 12, 2025, Thomas Keller, a dock worker, was invited to the Harborview office to assist with a temporary security audit. Using a USB drive, he accessed the firm’s internal network with stolen credentials from a phishing attack that had not yet been fully patched. He transferred encrypted client files to the drive and left it on a conference table. The IT manager discovered the drive at 12:00 pm and CCTV footage captured Keller leaving the office with the drive. Police were called at 1:00 pm, and Keller was apprehended. He later confessed via an email to his union.

timeline.event: Thomas Keller arrives at Harborview Law Partners for temporary audit
Unauthorized login to internal network using stolen credentials
Transfer of encrypted client files to USB drive
IT manager discovers USB drive on conference table
CCTV footage captures Keller leaving with drive

evidence.name: USB Drive
evidence.description: Encrypted client files found on conference table
evidence.truth_note: The drive was left by Keller as he exited; its presence on the table directly links him to the theft

evidence.name: CCTV Footage
evidence.description: Video showing Thomas Keller exiting the office with a USB drive
evidence.truth_note: The footage records Keller’s actions and confirms he carried the drive out of the premises

evidence.name: Email Log
evidence.description: Unauthorized login recorded from IP address linked to the dock terminal Keller uses
evidence.truth_note: The IP matches Keller’s dock workstation, indicating his use of stolen credentials

evidence.name: IT Manager Testimony
evidence.description: Sarah Lee reports seeing Keller leave with the USB drive and claims she was alerted by security protocols
evidence.bias: wants the firm to hold Keller accountable

evidence.name: Dock Supervisor Testimony
evidence.description: Mark Alvarez states Keller did not use any USB drive during his visit
evidence.bias: friendship with Keller; prefers to protect him
evidence.lie_reason: desire to shield Keller from prosecution

evidence.name: Software Anomaly Report
evidence.description: System reboot noted at 10:15 AM classified as anomaly
evidence.truth_note: The reboot was actually a scheduled maintenance event; the anomaly classification was an internal reporting oversight

evidence.name: Password Reset Log
evidence.description: Password changed at 10:10 AM, immediately after access began
evidence.truth_note: The change was an attempt by Keller to obscure the timing of his unauthorized activity

witnesses.name: Sarah Lee
witnesses.knows: Saw Thomas Keller leave with USB drive; aware of security protocols
witnesses.bias: wants the firm to hold Keller accountable

witnesses.name: Mark Alvarez
witnesses.knows: Thomas Keller was at the dock; denies use of USB drive
witnesses.bias: friendship with Keller; prefers to protect him
witnesses.lie_reason: desire to shield Keller from prosecution
